_readme: Labelled pitch sequences for the offline eval harness (src/lib/pitchEval.ts).
Each case pairs a generated sequence with the evidence it was supposed to be
built from, and states exactly which findings the scorer must produce. Change
a prompt in docs/pitch-research-prompts.json, a word target in
src/lib/pitchQuality.ts, or a check in the scorer, and the cases that flip
tell you what the change actually did.
Failure cases are drawn from things that have shipped or nearly shipped: a
generic opener that could have gone to any show, an invented guest name, a
strategy document pasted into a host-facing email, and a prior client named
on an episode that never aired.
expect_findings must list every finding id the scorer emits, in any order.
An empty list means the sequence is clean.
A label starting 'Fails' means at least one blocking finding — copy that must
never reach a host. 'Flags without blocking' is copy an operator should fix
before sending but which is not itself dangerous.

cases.label: Clean: opens on a real episode moment, right length, no tells

evidence.research: The Good, Bad & the Ugly of Self Storage is hosted by Michael Wagner. In the episode 'Buying at the top of the market' he spoke with Peter Smythe about paying too much for a facility in 2022 and what the workout looked like. Michael repeatedly returns to operators who bought badly and recovered.
episode_titles: Buying at the top of the market

sequence.subject: Your Peter Smythe episode
sequence.email_1: Hi Michael, your conversation with Peter Smythe about buying at the top of the market stuck with me, particularly the part where he walked through the workout rather than skipping to the happy ending. Most storage conversations stop at the acquisition and leave the hard year out entirely. I work with Dallas Fontaine, who took over three underwater facilities in 2023 and rebuilt occupancy without discounting rates, and he can talk through the specific decisions that worked as well as the two that did not. Would that be a fit for the show? Happy to send a few specifics first if it helps you judge.
sequence.follow_up_1: Hi Michael, following up on the note about Dallas Fontaine. One thing your listeners might find useful: he tracks the point at which a discount stops buying occupancy and starts buying churn. Worth a conversation?
sequence.follow_up_2: Hi Michael, I will stop here so I am not cluttering your inbox. If the timing is better later in the year, just say the word and I will come back then.
